result:
Turbonomic can help Unilever leverage AI for multi-cloud observability by providing a unified, automated platform that analyzes the entire infrastructure across different cloud providers. It uses AI to identify performance bottlenecks, optimize resource allocation, and ensure that applications are running efficiently. By providing a single pane of glass for multi-cloud environments, Turbonomic helps Unilever gain visibility into their infrastructure, identify potential issues before they occur, and make data-driven decisions about resource management.

The difference between Turbonomic and native tools from GCP, AWS, and Azure lies in their scope and capabilities. Native tools are designed to monitor and manage resources within their respective cloud platforms. While they provide deep insights into their specific environments, they lack the ability to provide a unified view of a multi-cloud infrastructure. Turbonomic, on the other hand, is designed to work across multiple cloud providers, providing a consistent and comprehensive view of the entire infrastructure. It also uses AI to automate many of the tasks that would otherwise require manual intervention, such as identifying and resolving performance issues and optimizing resource allocation.

function.name: get_weather_forecast
function.description: Retrieves the weather forecast for a specified location and date range. The forecast includes temperature, precipitation, and wind speed. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location for which the weather forecast is requested, in the format of 'City, Country' (e.g., 'London, UK').

start_date.description: The start date of the period for the weather forecast in the ISO 8601 format (e.g., '2023-04-01').

end_date.description: The end date of the period for the weather forecast in the ISO 8601 format (e.g., '2023-04-07').

units.description: The unit system in which to return the weather forecast data.

include_details.description: Specifies whether to include detailed forecast information such as humidity and visibility.
